text:
Anya: Heads-up — noticed oscillation in route selection for slo-tiered tenants after last week's penalty tweak. Two tenants flip between us-west and dedicated-pool-1 every ~30s. Can we discuss short-term mitigation and a clean long-term fix?
Matt: Can you paste a short example trace and which penalty you mean? Wasn't the change only to the region penalty normalization constant?
Anya: Trace snippet: tenant T-12 moves: us-west -> dedicated-pool-1 -> us-west -> dedicated... latency delta ~6ms, cost delta $0.0008/token. After normalization the score swings ~0.02 and hits tie-breaker. Current scoring:
```
route_score = base_score - penalty_region_ms * w_region - penalty_capacity_pct * w_capacity - cost_per_token * w_cost + affinity_bonus
```
Matt: got it. So mixed units cause fragility. We normalized each penalty independently but didn't enforce a global scale.
Priya: I ran a quick sim earlier. Root cause is heterogeneous scales + no hysteresis. Region penalty in ms ends up numerically large vs cost. Two options: 1) shared scale transform per-penalty (log/softplus) + learnable weights, or 2) switch to multiplicative penalties so units don't sum directly.
Kyle: Multiplicative sounds elegant but would change semantics heavily. Also harder to reason about rollbacks. Deterministic tie-breaker + cooldown might be lower-risk short-term.
Leah: Proposed short-term mitigation: add per-tenant cooldown (60-120s) before allowing route changes, and a deterministic tie-break by route id. Long-term: normalization function that compresses disparate units.
Anya: Concrete proposal:
1) Turn per-penalty normalization into a log-softplus scale so we operate on comparable magnitudes: normalized = softplus(log(1 + raw / scale))
2) Add route cooldown: per-tenant, per-route last_swap_ts and require delta >= cooldown_ms to switch unless delta_score > forced_threshold (2x default).
3) Introduce 'cost_budget' override for tenant-level routing to cap cost-driven switches.
Example config snippet: 
```
policies:
  - name: slo-tiered-default
    weights:
      region: 1.0
      capacity: 0.8
      cost: 0.6
    normalization:
      region: {type: "log_softplus", scale: 10}
      cost: {type: "log_softplus", scale: 0.0001}
    cooldown_ms: 90000
    forced_threshold: 0.04
```
Priya: I'll add a deterministic tie-breaker (stable route id) and implement a test that simulates the 30s oscillation to verify cooldown helps. Also we should ensure affinity shards don't reset cooldown globally. Cooldown must be shard-local.
Kyle: Agree on shard-local cooldown. Also watch for interactions with prefix/KV cache — route swaps can invalidate caches and spike latency. Maybe add a cache-invalidation-delay window to avoid immediate traffic on new route until warmed.
Leah: For telemetry, add a new event 'route_suppression' with fields: tenant_id, from_route, to_route, reason (cooldown|threshold|manual), cooldown_ms, score_delta. That will help quantify how many decisions we suppress.
Anya: From rollout perspective: plan = RFC followup today, simulation + unit tests by Priya, then canary deploy to policy-eval next week, monitor route churn and cost. If canary looks good, roll wide. Any objections?
Matt: No objections. Also need to update the policy-adapter interface: add normalized_penalties array and last_swap_ts in RouteState proto.
Priya: I'll own tests and the sim run. Will also add a regression that exercises affinity shard-local cooldown.
Kyle: One more thought — instead of multiplicative penalties, we could convert everything to a percentile rank (0-1) per-tenant historical distribution. That avoids unit mixing and keeps additive semantics. Worth a short spike.
Leah: Percentile conversion is nice but needs stable baselines and warmup. Might be best for long-term. Short-term do cooldown + log-softplus normalization.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: policy-eval-canary for RFC-2799 on 2026-05-07T03:00:00Z.
Anya: Thanks all — I'll draft the RFC follow-up with the config snippet + sim plan and ping for review.
